parts.watchFor: Musa stands before Pharaoh. Watch who believes, and who refuses no matter what.

questions.q: What happened to the magicians' ropes and staffs?
What did the magicians do when they saw it?
options: Fell down in prostration and believed

questions.q: What did Asiya, Pharaoh's wife, pray for?
options: A house near God in Paradise, and to be saved from Pharaoh

lesson.text: The magicians saw the truth and believed in a moment, whatever Pharaoh threatened. Asiya believed inside Pharaoh's own palace. Pharaoh saw sign after sign and broke his word each time. Faith means choosing the truth when you see it.
lesson.curious: Muslims honour the magicians who believed and Asiya, Pharaoh's wife, who chose faith despite Pharaoh's power. Pharaoh is the warning: he saw the signs and refused.

reflect.muslim: When did you last see the truth about something and not act on it?
reflect.curious: What makes it hard to admit you were wrong, especially in front of others?

parts.act: When you realise you were wrong about something this week, say so straight away.

parts.watchFor: Pharaoh's army chases them to the sea. Watch what Musa says when everyone panics.

questions.q: What did the people cry when they saw the army?

options: No! My Lord is with me; He will guide me

questions.q: What did Musa do on the far shore?
options: Bowed down in thanks to the One who saved them

lesson.text: With the sea ahead and an army behind, Musa said: my Lord is with me; He will guide me. Trust, then do what you're told: strike the sea. And belief must come in time: Pharaoh's came too late.
lesson.curious: The crossing of the sea is told in the Quran and the Bible. Muslims draw from Musa's words a model of trust when there seems to be no way out.

reflect.muslim: What feels like a sea in front of you right now? What is your staff, the thing you can do?
reflect.curious: When have you felt trapped with no way out? What helped?

parts.act: Next time you panic, stop and say: my Lord is with me; He will guide me.
